C-44, ss. 140.1-140.7 (federal registered beneficial owner regime); applicable provincial limited partnership statutes for UBO and registry disclosure, including Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, directors, and authorized signatories against FINTRAC politically exposed person (PEP) categories and close associates/family members; sanctions screening must include the United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, Canadian sanctions regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, the United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-17, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), S.C. 2017, c. 21, and, where any USD clearing or US payment rail is involved, the OFAC SDN List. Any direct or indirect match triggers automatic escalation, enhanced due diligence, and senior management approval; permitted PEPs require ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada / NUANS Name Search and Name Reservation Portal (https://www.nuans.com), operated by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada; integrated with provincial corporate registries for extra-provincial limited partnership registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Official Languages Act, federal-level entity names may be in English, French, or bilingual form; the legal element must appear as Limited Partnership, L.P., Société en Commandite, or S.E.C. depending on the language version. Names must use Latin script with official diacritical marks where applicable; non-Latin transliterations are not accepted. The name must be distinct from all existing registered names, business names, and registered trademarks in Canada, and must not cause confusion with a recognized institution or government entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director of Corporations Canada or the delegated provincial registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to Corporations Canada within 30 days of the refusal, attaching a new NUANS search, consent letters from any conflicting rights holders, trademark registrations, or other evidence of distinctiveness. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may request written reasons and apply to the Federal Court for judicial review under section 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-7. Parallel provincial appeal procedures apply where the limited partnership is registered extra-provincially. Administrative fees are payable at each stage, and a fresh name reservation may be filed immediately without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a federally tax-registered limited partnership operating a digital video-matching app, a virtual office is acceptable only as a registered office for service of process and statutory records; it does not by itself create commercial substance for Canadian corporate presence. Apple IAP and Paymentwall payment rails do not require local physical infrastructure, but a pure mailbox address may be rejected by Canadian financial institutions, FINTRAC-supervised payment intermediaries, or provincial registries. A serviced office or co-working space with an active Canadian agent is recommended to satisfy commercial substance expectations, particularly for GST/HST registration, income tax residency analysis, and bank account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Baseline unannounced physical inspection probability in the first 24 months is approximately 20-25%. If enhanced due diligence is triggered by PEP/sanctions hits, high-risk jurisdiction payment routing, incomplete UBO documentation, or unexplained nominee structures, the probability rises to 40-50%. Canadian Revenue Agency and FINTRAC examinations may occur on-site, and a virtual registered office increases the likelihood of a compliance visit where records cannot be produced promptly.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada does not provide a federal limited partnership statute; the limited partnership is constituted under a provincial Limited Partnerships Act (e.g., Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.7, ss. 2, 8, 9-10), while a corporate general partner is formed under the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 16, 21; federal tax identifiers (Business Number, GST/HST, and payroll) are governed by the Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15, s. 241, and the Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) for the federal general partner and Business Number; provincial companies registry (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Branch) for the Certificate of Limited Partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Limited Partnership (provincial filing), together with the federal Form RC1 - Request for a Business Number (CRA) and, where applicable, Articles of Incorporation (CBCA Form 1) for the corporate general partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Partners may contribute cash, property, or services as agreed in the partnership agreement; no escrow account is required before registration, provided that the limited partners' capital contributions are actually made or contractually undertaken to preserve limited liability.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the board of the general partner approves the formation of [●] Limited Partnership (the 'Partnership') under the applicable Limited Partnerships Act; that the Certificate of Limited Partnership be executed and filed with the provincial registry; that the registered office be established in Ontario and its address be filed; that [●] hereby be appointed sole general partner and [●], [●], [●] be admitted as initial limited partners; that the Partnership Agreement presented to this board be adopted; that the Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and applicable GST/HST and payroll accounts be obtained; and that the officers and directors are jointly and severally authorized to execute all documents and take all steps necessary to complete formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (NUANS search system), administered through provincial registries and authorized service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS corporate name search request for the proposed limited partnership name and ensure it is not confusingly similar to existing federal or provincial names; if the selected governing province offers name reservation, reserve the name for the statutory term (up to 90 days).
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS search request (name, entity type, jurisdiction)
NUANS name search report
Proof of name reservation (where issued)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion, submit a revised name through the same portal; refiling is processed as a new request with a reduced service standard of one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Partnership Agreement and General Partner Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and the board of directors of the corporate general partner (no government window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement covering capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, management authority, withdrawal, admission, and dissolution; hold the first board meeting of the general partner and pass the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution approving the Partnership Agreement, registered office, and officer appointments.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement
Pro-Forma First Board Resolution
Conflict-of-interest disclosure statements
Certified copies of the general partner's incorporating documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any drafting defect is cured by executing an amending partnership agreement before registration; re-execution must be unanimous among the partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the Certificate of Limited Partnership (Provincial Statutory Registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial companies registry (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Branch)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the executed Certificate of Limited Partnership (or prescribed statement) with the governing provincial registry; pay the statutory filing fee; the registry endorses the certificate and issues proof of registration establishing the limited partnership's existence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership (signed by all initial limited partners and the general partner)
Filing fee payment confirmation
Name search certificate or reservation
If applicable, certified copy of the general partner's articles of incorporation and good standing certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the filing is queried or rejected for deficiency, file a corrected or amended certificate; on confirmation of consistency with provincial forms being achieved, re-file through the same registry window without additional fee within the notice period described in the registry's deficiency letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Registration with the Canada Revenue Agency (Business Number, GST/HST and Payroll Accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for a federal Business Number through CRA's Business Registration Online; open a GST/HST account if taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold, and open payroll (RP) and import/export accounts as required; register each partner and the general partner's ownership structure in the CRA system.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
Registered office address and mailing address
General partner's Business Number and incorporation number
List of all partners with citizenship and residency status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA rejects or freezes the registration for missing information, respond to the notice through My Business Account, submit the corrected declaration, and request reconsideration; reassessment is normally completed within ten business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of each Canadian province or territory where the partnership carries on business (e.g., BC Corporate Online, Alberta Corporate Registry, Registraire des entreprises Quebec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the partnership will carry on business outside its governing province, file an application for extra-provincial registration in each such province; appoint an attorney for service of process resident in that province; remit the provincial registration fee and obtain the extra-provincial registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Certified true copy of the Certificate of Limited Partnership
Certificate of good standing (or equivalent) from the governing province
Enduring power of attorney appointing resident attorney for service
Notice of registered extra-provincial office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings attract penalty tariffs; cure by filing the outstanding extra-provincial registration and paying the recovery fee, after which the registry issues the certificate retroactively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance, Bank Account, and Annual Compliance Calendaring
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial institutions, the general partner's board, and the governing provincial registry / CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the partnership's bank account using the Certificate of Limited Partnership and CRA Business Number; update the minute book of the general partner; requisition the CRA program accounts; calendar the provincial annual declaration (if applicable) and the CRA annual information return; order the official partnership seal and certified copies for bank and counterparty use.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
CRA Business Number confirmation
Partnership Agreement
General partner's board resolutions on banking and signing authorities
KYC / AML records for each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or counterparty refuses documents, obtain a certificate of compliance from the provincial registry and a supplementary good standing certificate, then resubmit; internal governance defects are cured by subsequent unanimous resolutions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - a real-time video-matching social telephony service under ISIC 6311 (web portals / data processing) is not subject to a federal industrial or manufacturing licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no operating license, manufacturing permit, or broadcasting certification is required at the federal level for a real-time video-matching platform that does not carry on broadcasting or telecommunications common-carrier activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / Impact Assessment Agency of Canada
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity is a digital platform with no physical works; no designated project under the Impact Assessment Act, S.C. 2019, c. 28, s. 1, and its Physical Activities Regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial discharge; if the operator hosts servers, comply with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 (S.C. 1999, c. 33) for e-waste export, ozone-depleting substances from cooling equipment, and municipal wastewater and stormwater discharge limits in the hosting province; any data-centre tenancy must meet the Canadian Electrical Code (C22.1) and ASHRAE thermal guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the head-office tenancy, obtain fire safety clearance under the National Fire Code - 2020 (NFC) and the local fire marshal's inspection certificate; maintain worker health and safety board coverage (e.g., WSIB in Ontario) under the applicable provincial occupational health and safety act; structural load inspection is not applicable for a standard office lease, but leased premises must display a valid occupancy certificate from the local building authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; taxpayer portal: CRA My Business Account (MyBA) at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity obtaining a statutory tax identity must apply for a CRA Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or using the 'Register a business' online service. For a Canadian Limited Partnership, the general partner files the application in the partnership's name, designates partnership capacity, and provides the registered address, jurisdiction of formation, list of partners, and anticipated taxable supplies paid. If GST/HST registration is required, the CRA will assign a dedicated GST/HST account number. A non-resident limited partner need not obtain a separate BN solely for the partnership, but the general partner must act as the agent of the partnership for all tax administration matters.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' election; a Limited Partnership is statutorily treated as a pass-through entity under subsection 96(1) of the Income Tax Act, with partners computing their own income shares. Available election mechanisms include: (i) the partnership admission election under subsection 97(2) of the Income Tax Act to deem a fair market value transfer to the partnership; (ii) the GST/HST joint venture election under section 273 of the Excise Tax Act allowing a partner to be the operator for GST/HST purposes; and (iii) hybrid mismatch recharacterization adjustments under sections 93.5 and 93.6 of the Income Tax Act for cross-border payments, limiting deductible amounts where there is a hybrid payee or payment character mismatch.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (including taxable supplies made in Canada and by non-resident digital service providers) in any four consecutive calendar quarters; once exceeded, mandatory GST/HST registration applies. A smaller threshold applies to transporters and non-residents carrying on a commercial activity in Canada that supplies real property in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate a national real-time electronic invoicing or fiscal clearance system. CRA accepts electronic invoices and records under the GST/HST electronic record requirements, provided they are in an accessible format and permit accurate verification. There is no digital stamping or API-based pre-clearance for GST/HST returns; however, registrants must file GST/HST returns electronically through CRA's electronic services and maintain complete audit trails. For cross-border digital services, non-resident suppliers may be required to register under the simplified non-resident GST/HST registration framework and file returns through CRA's e-services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods qualify for zero-rating when they are exported by the supplier or a related intermediary and shipped directly to a destination outside Canada, with the supplier retaining continuous export evidence. Services qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is a non-resident person at the time the consideration becomes due and the service is not performed for an individual present in Canada, does not relate to real estate located in Canada, and is not a service of rendering tangible personal property situated in Canada. For the described video-match social app, a supply of online digital services to a non-resident user will generally be zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, provided the service is not delivered to a person in Canada and the supplier can demonstrate the non-resident status of the user through payment routing, IP address geolocation, and user subscription data.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency form B13A or authorized electronic export reporting declaration)
Bill of Lading (through bill of lading or multimodal transport document evidencing physical movement of goods from Canada to a foreign destination)
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank wire / SWIFT confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency proceeds into a Canadian bank account)
Commercial invoice and purchase contract/purchase order from the non-resident buyer
Non-resident status evidence of the digital service recipient, including IP address logs, billing address, and subscription records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may audit exporters and deny zero-rating where documentation is incomplete. Retrospective reassessment within the normal four-year limitation period (or longer in cases of misrepresentation or fraud) will impose GST/HST at 5% on the previously zero-rated supply, together with compound interest on arrears. Civil penalties under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act may reach the greater of CAD 500 and 25% of the tax sought to be evaded, with additional penalties for repeated false statements of up to CAD 25,000. Fraudulent export schemes may result in criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. All input tax credits originally claimed on underlying expenses for zero-rated exports are subject to clawback if the zero-rating is reversed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential banking supervision is shared with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money-laundering and cross-border currency transaction reporting is administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). No separate foreign-exchange control administration exists because Canada has maintained a freely floating, fully convertible currency since the abolition of exchange controls in 1951.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies to both current and capital accounts under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act. CAD/USD and all major-currency pairs are unrestricted. Non-resident limited partners may remit profits and capital without foreign-exchange approval; however, distributions characterized as partnership income bear Part XIII withholding tax (treaty-reduced, typically 15% for US limited partners under the Canada-US Tax Convention), and all currency movements above CAD 10,000 require FINTRAC reporting. In-bound subscription and IAP receipts are freely remittable as business income, subject to normal Canadian income tax for the partnership and to transfer-pricing documentation where non-resident partners are involved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no conversion timeline exist in Canada. Exporters and cross-border service providers may retain foreign currency indefinitely. The only mandatory obligations are FINTRAC reports for cross-border currency transfers equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000, anti-money-laundering record-keeping under the PCMLTFA, and information returns (Form T2063/T106 as applicable) for partnership distributions to non-residents.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Canada does not recognize the UK/EU electronic-money-institution (EMI) licence as a deposit-taking authorization; an offshore EMI may be used as a secondary collection corridor but cannot serve as the entity's principal regulated bank account. For digital revenue settlement, the preferable structure is a federal Schedule I bank operating account supplemented by a FINTRAC-registered money-services-business (MSB) licence or a Payments-Canada-member payment facilitator. The target rails (Apple IAP and Paymentwall) function as merchants of record, so settlement flows arrive as depository payouts rather than direct card-acquiring; this reduces payment-licensing friction but adds a reconciliation layer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default mandate for all authorized signatories and for the corporate General Partner's authorized representative. Several Schedule I banks permit fully remote onboarding using enhanced video-verification and notarized documents, but a Canadian Limited Partnership with non-resident partners and a novel high-volume digital business will typically trigger enhanced due diligence (EDD), requiring a live interview with the compliance officer. At minimum, the General Partner must be identified, and every individual with significant control (25% or greater economic interest) must pass identity verification before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: a Limited Partnership structure with non-resident partners and a corporate General Partner can be misclassified as a shell-risk entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed limited partnership agreement; certificate of limited partnership and annual registration extracts; register of individuals with significant control; General Partner corporate KYC package (certificate of good standing, constitutional documents, board resolution appointing signatories); source-of-funds letters prepared by each committed partner; capital-call documentation matching the injection schedule; and a written group-structure diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border social-telephony and random-video-matching risk: perceived exposure to anonymous users, adult-content risk, and high-refund chargeback patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC-compliant AML/ATF program; written risk assessment and transaction-monitoring rules; user age-verification and identity-assurance policy; content-moderation and prohibited-use policy; PIPEDA-compliant privacy program; app-store terms of service; and merchant-of-record agreements demonstrating that platform regulatory liability is contractually allocated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and geolocation risk: a global real-time matching application may inadvertently serve sanctioned jurisdictions or blocked persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP-address and geolocation blocking of sanctioned territories; automated sanctions screening against OSFI, UN, US OFAC, and EU lists; adverse-media monitoring; contractual prohibition on use from sanctioned countries; periodic independent testing of screening controls; and a sanctions-compliance attestation signed by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-flow opacity: settlement through Apple IAP and Paymentwall creates a payer-of-record and payout-lag structure that can appear as third-party payment intermediation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Apple Developer Program and Paymentwall merchant agreements; monthly payout reconciliation reports by transaction; platform fee and net-settlement schedules; audited financial statements for the Limited Partnership; cash-flow projections explaining treasury requirements; and documentation confirming that platform settlement funds are held in the operating account for treasury purposes only, not as custodial client funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: SWIFT MT103 with remittance information tagged 'Limited Partnership Capital Contribution – [Partner Legal Name]'. No Bank of Canada pre-approval or purpose-code registration is required; however, the receiving bank must hold the executed capital-call notice, the limited partnership agreement annexure, and a beneficial-ownership attestation. Non-resident CAD funds are cleared directly through Payments Canada's Lynx system; USD funds are routed via the bank's US correspondent (New York branch) using ABA and Fedwire or CHIPS. FINTRAC suspicious-transaction reporting and large-transaction reporting above CAD 10,000 apply; all supporting documentation must be retained for a minimum of five years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for international vendor and partner disbursements; (2) Payments Canada Lynx (successor to LVTS) for high-value CAD wires; (3) commercial letters of credit issued through the bank's trade desk for goods-based import settlements; (4) USD disbursements via correspondent banking through Fedwire and CHIPS; (5) batch payout APIs (RBC Global Payments, CIBC Money Management, BMO Global Transaction Banking) for user and creator commission settlements. SWIFT narrative fields must remain within the 'Remittance Information' character limit, and every USD wire equivalent to CAD 10,000 or more must carry a FINTRAC reportable transaction record.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/CAD FX forwards (standard tenors up to 24 months)
European-style USD/CAD FX options (purchased and covered written)
USD/CAD cross-currency swaps (fixed-to-fixed or basis swaps)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-currency exposures such as CNY, INR, or RUB where convertibility is limited
Exchange-traded USD/CAD futures on the Montréal Exchange or CME

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 60 days after the anniversary of the limited partnership's formation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to $200 per day; administrative dissolution possible after 90 days of non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit required only if gross revenue exceeds CAD 1,000,000 or if the partnership agreement mandates an audit

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information is required upon any change in ownership structure; no routine annual filing unless changes occur

stage_6.entry_description: Aggregate gross revenue from the video-match social platform (subscriptions, Apple IAP settlements, Paymentwall receivables) less allowable business expenses (hosting, bandwidth, content moderation, payment processing fees, IP royalties paid).
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners' share must be computed in Canadian dollars and based on the partnership's Canadian-source business income; foreign exchange gains/losses are accounted for under s.39(1)?
